utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, could you call the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll now ask the Prosecution to introduce themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Counsel. For the Prosecution, I would like to introduce Mr. Chester Stamp on my right-hand side; otherwise, Daryl Mundis, Ekkehard Withopf, and Kimberly Fleming as the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. My name is Edina Residovic. I represent General Hadzihasanovic, and I'm assisted by Stephane Bourgon, from Montreal, and Mirna Milanovic, the legal assistant. Stephane Bourgon is co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. Fahrudin Ibrisimovic; my legal assistant, Mr. Mulalic, represent Mr. Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Trial Chamber greets everyone who is present here, the Prosecution, the Defence, and the accused. Before the Prosecution takes the floor to hear the witness, I have to inform you that the hearing of tomorrow will be finished at 11.00 because there is another trial which is scheduled for 11.30. And given the schedule, we will have to stop at 11.00. There is no other way. There are only three courtrooms, as you know. There are six ongoing trials at the same time, and the trial tomorrow has to start at 11.30, which is why we will have to conclude at 11.00. As far as the Defence is concerned, I would like to address the Defence with regard to the motion for access to archives of the UN. In Annex B of your document - it's on page 6; it finishes at paragraph 17 - was there a paragraph 18 or 19, or does it end at paragraph -- on page 6 of paragraph 17?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. Unfortunately, I don't have the information with me. But I have taken note of what you have said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I can provide you with the document that I have and you will be able to examine it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the last paragraph of Annex B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there is no paragraph number 18?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, the Trial Chamber shall render its decision in the course of the afternoon. We will make a ruling in the course of the afternoon, which will be forwarded to the Registry, and you will immediately be informed of it. There is a third issue I would like to raise, which concerns witnesses and protective measures required -- requested by the Prosecution. I thought it would be desirable if the Prosecution, who has a schedule for witnesses, knows in advance which witnesses will be requiring protective measures. Without advising the Prosecution in any way, it seems to me that it would be useful to point out to the Prosecution that given that there is already a schedule, a witness schedule, the Prosecution could contact the witnesses by phone or send them a letter two or three weeks in advance to find out whether they require protective measures, because, as far as I have understood the matter, we will be presented with an oral request for protective measures at the very last minute. Perhaps there is a reason. Obviously there are financial reasons. The witnesses arrive on a day and you have an interview with them, you speak to them, and they may require protective measures at that time. But if there is a contact over the phone, in such a case there would be no problems. Secondly, as far as protective measures are concerned, the Trial Chamber would like these requests to be made in writing, and it also seems to me that it would be useful if these requests also stated whether the witnesses in their national jurisdictions, whether they have already appeared before their national courts, because if they have already testified in a national court without protective measures, I do not understand why they would require protective measures at this Tribunal. So it would be interesting to know what their situation is, if that is possible, with regard to their rights. Because you must know what their personal situation is. If they have already been heard before a court and protective measures were not granted, there is no reason for them to be grant those measures here in this Tribunal. So it would be use to know what the situation is. Having read the schedule, I also see that we are a little late because the witness who had been scheduled are not appearing at the time they are scheduled for. So I would like to point this out to both parties. With regard to the production of -- the presentation of evidence y the Prosecution, the Prosecution's case should be completed at the end of May or in the course of June, but given the way we are proceeding this might be delayed. So I would like to draw your attention to the fact that this is an issue. There is a witness who has requested -- for whom protective measure wills be orally requested, so I am going to ask the Prosecution to take the floor. But I would like to point out that the Defence has only found out about this a few minutes ago. I don't know the reasons for this but the Prosecution will tell us what the reasons for this are. But I would like to ask Madam Registrar to go into private session, since a request is going to be made for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please ask the usher to bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, can you hear me in a language that you can understand? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. Witness, before you give the solemn declaration, I would like to tell you that the Prosecution has requested protective measures for you. The Defence has objected to that. The Trial Chamber has deliberated and decided that there is no valid reason for the protective measures to be granted to you. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. You are now going to make -- to give us your name and the date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zarko Jandric. I was born on the 2nd of April, 1964 in Grahovcici in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what is your profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am retired, for medical grounds. Before that, I was a metalworker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. And where do you currently reside, or the region where you currently reside.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I currently reside where I resided before. I returned to Grahovcici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can you then read the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You may be seated. Witness, you are now going to be asked questions by the Prosecution. And after that, the Defence is going to ask you questions. And after that, the Prosecution may ask you a few questions again, and the Judges also can ask you a few question. Have you understood that? I would like to remind you that you have to respond in line of what you know. You have to respond truthfully. You have to tell the truth. If you think that the answers that you are going to give could incriminate you, you can refuse to answer the question. So you are a free witness. You can answer as you wish. But when you do answer, we expect you to tell the truth. Did you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I give the floor to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would ask for the assistance of the usher, if he could perhaps move the ELMO so that I could see the witness. Thank you. Examined by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in response to questions from the Presiding Judge, you indicated you were born in Grahovcici and that you currently live in that same location. Have you lived in that village your entire life?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: No. I lived in that village until the beginning of the war. Then I was a refugee. I lived in Nova Bila and in Vitez with my family. During the war, they remained in Vitez and then for a while they lived in Busovaca. And as for myself, after I was wounded on the 12th of June, on the 20th of June I was transferred to the Republic of Croatia for treatment. After that, I returned in 1995 -- that is, to Vitez. I returned to Vitez. And as for Grahovcici, I returned to Grahovcici once my house was refurbished, and that was in 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever serve in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first join the HVO ?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of April I was formally -- I formally became a member. And then in May I assumed my first duties with the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you first assigned with the HVO and what were your primary duties?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: My first duties with the HVO concerned providing security for the barracks. That was in 1992 in Travnik. I had about 15 men under me who belonged to my unit. I was their commander. I was the commander to these 15 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe for the Trial Chamber where your unit was based in Travnik and which other military units were based at that location.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: The barracks is located almost in the very centre of the town, looking from Turbe, and it is still there. And there were units of the army and the HVO together. The military police were there as well. At the same time, we also accepted and received expelled Bosnians from Jajce, Krajina, and other places which had already been struck by the war and which had already been the area of conflict between Bosniaks and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The barracks that you've told us about, located in the very centre of the town, was that the former JNA barracks in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. It used to belong to the JNA, and it was taken from them, from the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told us, Witness, that in your words, there were units of the army and the HVO together. When you used the word "army," can you describe what army that was.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the members of the Bosniak armed units that belonged to different groups. They were still members of the army and of the Territorial Defence of various militia units. Within the barracks, there was also a detention unit. This is where -- the location that we shared. The command staff was also there at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the HVO and the Armija have a common enemy in May 1992, when you were in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: At that time, yes. There were no open conflicts in any of the parts where I resided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain with the HVO at the former JNA barracks in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: I remained there for a very short time, less than seven days, and then I was replaced by somebody else. Again, they were members of the HVO. And after that, I never stayed in that barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go, Witness, after you left the JNA barracks in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: We had organised shifts that involved also the former JNA barracks. We also had some positions on the lines facing the Serbs. So I did my regular shift, and then I returned to my place of residence, that is, to the village of Grahovcici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm a bit confused, Witness. You told us that you were only in Travnik for about seven days; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. During that particular shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you returned to your village of Grahovcici, after being in Travnik for seven days; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What month and year was it when you returned to Grahovcici?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: It was in 1992, the second half of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain in Grahovcici or its immediate vicinity after returning there in the second half of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: This is where I lived at that time. And from there I would go to certain front lines, to the then-positions facing the Serbs. Several times I went to the positions in Godjevica [phoen], Vlasic, Stolac, and other positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you about that in a moment, Witness. But first, can you tell us, please, approximately how far is Grahovcici from Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: The distance is about 23 kilometres, Grahovcici-Travnik. And Grahovcici is on a slope on the mountain of Ovnak. This is actually at the border between the municipalities of Zenica and Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is Grahovcici from the city of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: The distance between the entry to Zenica and Grahovcici is about 14 to 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If one were to draw an imaginary line from Zenica to Travnik, Grahovcici would be somewhere in between; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, a bit closer to Zenica. Before the war, we all used to go to school and we all worked in Zenica, because Zenica is closer. Although my village belonged to the municipality of Travnik formally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in May 1992, approximately how many people lived in the village of Grahovcici?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: According to the 1990 census, there were about 1.240 villagers and about 246 households.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of the village of Grahovcici in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Grahovcici was inhabited by Croats. Before the war, there was just one Serb family, counting -- a total of five Serbs living in Grahovcici, according to the last census.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, witness, if there were any Muslim families living in Grahovcici in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please name for the Trial Chamber any villages which would be between 3 and 5 kilometres away from Grahovcici.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Grahovcici has a number of neighbouring villages. If we start with Travnik municipality, then there is Klarici village, Dolac Bila, Han Bila, Brajkovici, Cukle, Susanj, Konjevici, further on, Pojske Paratje, Versalaj [phoen], and then if you go towards Zenica there are a number of bigger and smaller villages and hamlets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, upon your arrival back in Grahovcici in late May 1992, what military duties did you have with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: I was constantly engaged because I was still the platoon commander. After a certain time, I became the commander of a company, although I did not have the adequate training for that. However, the superior command appointed me to that duty, and from then on I had daily tasks with the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you indicated that you were the commander of a company. Can you tell us what company you commanded and which brigade that company was a member of.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: At the time of the existence of the Travnik Brigade, I was the commander of a platoon. When the Frankopan Brigade was established, I became company commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which company you commanded?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: It was the 1st Platoon of the 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once the Frankopan Brigade was established, what unit did you command?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: It was the 1st Company of the 2nd Battalion of the Frankopan Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the approximate month and year when the Frankopan Brigade was established?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: The Frankopan Brigade was established sometime in April 1993. It was the end of March or beginning of April. That was actually the re-establishment of the Travnik Brigade. The Travnik Brigade was reorganised into two different HVO brigades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the area of responsibility of the company that you commanded, the 1st Company, 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: In 1992 -- up to the end of 1992 and the beginning of 1993, the areas of responsibility were such that we would be sent to the positions facing the Serbian lines. For example, I had a shift in October 1992 on the Vlasenica Plateau, in the vicinity of the BH army towards Sasici. We linked up with the BH army positions at that time. Later on we would go to other positions, such as Godjevica [phoen] and some other positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did there come a time when your unit was more or less permanently stationed in the area of Grahovcici?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. The time did come when there were -- there was an increased number of conflicts between the army and the HVO, and that was in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe briefly for the Trial Chamber what you mean by "an increased number of conflicts between the army and the HVO" in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that we were stationed on Ovnak, this was a strategic position that was of general interest for both the HVO and the army. It happened at that time that people who returned from their shifts, from the lines facing the Serbs, would be searched, would be stopped at checkpoints, and this escalated and thus made the relationship between the army and the HVO worse by the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What eventually happened between the army and the HVO in the Grahovcici area, beginning from, say, May 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: What happened did not just happen overnight. The relationship gradually got worse after the killing of Ivica Stojak, who were the commander of our brigade. And then in Zenica, Totic was kidnapped. And after that, all the roads were blocked. And from then on we reached an impasse and we were encircled, we were constantly encircled. And from then on we didn't go to the lines facing the Serbs. Rather, we started digging trenches and we started reinforcing positions around our own villages and around our own houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Witness, when there was active conflict between the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO in the area of Grahovcici?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: This happened a bit later, and conflicts culminated in June 1993. Before that, there were conflicts between the army and the HVO in Zenica. A number of refugees, both the military and the civilians arrived in our village, and some actually passed through our village to go to Vitez, Nova Bila, and Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when did the conflict begin in the city of Zenica, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: The kidnapping of commander Zivko Totic happened in May 1993, and conflicts started sop five days later, in the general area of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe for the Chamber the situation in the Grahovcici area from the time of the kidnapping of Zivko Totic onwards.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: After that incident, during the night or early in the morning refugees would come from Zenica municipality. Those were Croats. Brigade Francetic and their commander, Ljubicic, were relocated towards Osunjca and towards our village in my area of responsibility. And then sometime around mid-May everybody moved to the area of Travnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at this point in time, late spring/early summer 1993, what was the area of responsibility of your company, the company that you commanded?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: I've already said that in the Frankopan Brigade I was given a bigger area of responsibility as company commander. This area of responsibility was my village, from Dolac, Rudnik to Ovnak, to the crossroads on Ovnak. But at that time we had on our strengths several smaller units from the Francetic Brigade. I'm talking about the time from the month of May onwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in May of 1993, was there any fighting in the area around Ovnak?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was an attack against the position in Cice, which is above the inhabited places of Ovnak and Cukle. And on the 23rd of May, there was a murder, Nikola Bilic was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Nikola Bilic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Nikola Bilic was a small private businessman. He had his own shop. He would usually take cigars -- he would often take cigars to the soldiers in the trenches. And on one such occasion he was hit from the direction of Konjevici. He was hit in the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at the time Nikola Bilic was shot, who controlled Ovnak?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: We were still controlling Ovnak. It was under the control of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the HVO control Ovnak?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Up until the 8th of June, when the entire area, all the inhabited places, Zupa, Brajkovici and Biljanska Reka, which is where the Croats lived, they -- these places were taken and they were expelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time in late May or early June 1993, did the HVO temporarily lose control of Ovnak?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Not of Ovnak, but over the position of Usce, yes, they did lose control. For a very brief period of time that position was taken, but it was recaptured on the same day. And on that position there were two captured members of the HVO and a member of the BH army, who was killed, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present on Usce on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: At the time, no, I wasn't. But I was given the commander to go to the site and to see what happened in the course of the attack and after the position had been recaptured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall anything that you discovered when you went to Use on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: When I arrived at the position, where HV members were present, again I found the dead body of a BH army member. We knew him from before, because he was from the surrounding -- a surrounding Bosniak village, in the vicinity of Pojske. We found some papers on him, and I forwarded them to the command. There were documents, a list of Muslim armed forces. There were about 15 names and surnames and certain other items, reserve rations, food, a rifle, ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember or recall which unit this individual who was killed was with?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: He was a member of the so-called 8th Muslim Armed Forces. At the time, I don't know the exact structure, but these were elite units of the Muslim army. He was from the MOS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the acronym MOS stands for, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: All I know is that it means the Muslim Armed Forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe for the Trial Chamber the situation as it existed in Grahovcici and the area surrounding that village from late May 1993, the military situation.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: At the end of May and up to the beginning of June, the situation deteriorated from day to day with regard to the positions that we held and also with regard to taking in displaced Croats from the municipality of Zenica and obtaining supplies of food. We frequently contacted UNPROFOR forces, and on several occasions we even received food for the expelled people. But on the battle lines there were sporadic shooting on a daily basis, either for short or long periods of time. Firearms were used. And this situation continued up until the beginning of June, when the attacks intensified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe the attacks that intensified in the beginning of June.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: These attacks were mostly carried out with light and heavy firearms from Tolnica, Brda, from the direction of Klajca [phoen]. There was a large-scale attack carried out by the -- carried out on the 5th of 6th. On that occasion, I lost a soldier at that position. There were eight wounded, but we managed to recapture those positions that had been taken. At that time, we were already completely surrounded, and we couldn't evacuate the wounded. We would just take them to a temporary clinic which was located in a house, Jozo Sika's house in Grahovcici. We waited for nightfall there and then we would evacuate them to Sarici and further on, in an improvised hospital in Bila and in -- in Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the first week of June 1993, where was your unit deployed? In what specific area?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Up until the 8th of June, our units weren't moved from the fortified lines around the village itself. Each trench that was taken meant that the army forces were directly entering the village. So our military forces did not move at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far were the trenches from the village of Grahovcici itself?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: It depends on the position you look at it from. From the Milka and Ovnak-inhabited places, these were fortified places. There were trenches in front of the houses themselves, whereas at the Strmac position and at Usce position, the distance from the houses was between 1 to 2 kilometres. It depended on the lie of the land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, witness, you mentioned "up until the 8th of June." Can you tell the Trial Chamber what happened on the 8th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of June, although we knew from reconnaissance that had been carried out earlier on and from observation of BH army movement, there was a synchronised attack directed at the entire area of Zupa Brajkovici, and all the Croatian villages in that territory of mine. In the early morning hours, this attack was carried out from about four directions. That attack was carried out primarily from the direction of Usce, Crni Vrh, and Cukle. And the forces were directed from Ovnak, and also from Petcanica [phoen] and Strmac. But as the situation developed, from the direction of Pojske and Konjevici, it was directed towards the centre of the village, towards Milka and Vrbica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which force or forces were carrying out this attack?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: It was a large-scale attack carried out by the BH army, in cooperation with BH army forces from the municipality of Zenica and Travnik, because the attack was carried out simultaneously from several directions. I was able to follow the way the situation unfolded very well because I was at an elevated position, a little less than a thousand metres away, at the Strmac position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see happening on the morning of the 8th of June, 1993, from this elevated position that you've told us about?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: In the early morning hours, first of all there was an attack at that position in Usce from the Paratje-Pojske directions. And there was an attack from the direction of Mehurici and Travnik, directed at Orasac and Cukle. These positions first fell into the hands of the army, and then in a short period of time there was an attack directed against Sminjaca and Strmac. So by about 11.00 my position -- my place and all other Croatian villages -- my village and all other Croatian villages had been attacked by all directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at this time, 11.00 on the 8th of June, 1993, how many HVO soldiers were in the village of Grahovcici itself?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: In Grahovcici there were -- the regular HVO units were there. But soldiers and the civilian population were moved from the direction of Cukle and Orasac, and they kept arriving in Ovnak and Grahovcici, so that the number of soldiers in Grahovcici increased. And also the entire civilian population, entire villages would arrive in Grahovcici and we would provide them with shelter from the constant shelling during the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to this -- these refugees who had gathered in Grahovcici as the armed conflict progressed on the 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: We had people who were responsible in the civilian protection, and from the time that Zenica fell they took care of the displaced civilians and they provided them with accommodation. They were provided with accommodation, with houses and schools and in the direction of Kopaca, where they weren't that exposed to the shelling the and the attacks. And this was the case up until the 13th, when Marko Jerkic came to see me - he became the commander of the civilian protection - and Jozo Cuturic came to see me, about evacuating the civilian population towards Nova Bila. There were quite a few who had been wounded and quite a few who had been killed. There were women and children there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how long did the fighting continue in Grahovcici on the 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: The fighting in Grahovcici continued until the early evening hours, and that position was the last one to be taken, the Strmac position. And in the early evening hours we had to withdraw from that position towards Cekine Kuce, Cekine houses, towards the position of inhabited places of Balance [phoen] and Brce [phoen]. And at that time, the civilian population had been evacuated to those places and they were fleeing and there were over 4.000 people who were fleeing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, from the elevated position that you told us about a few moments ago, were you witnessing the fighting that was going on in Grahovcici throughout the day of the 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part. I had an entire part of Ovnak in my field of vision and part of Cukle and the entire village of Brajkovici. It was the village That's an elevated position from which you can see a lot. And I also had a pair of binoculars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time, roughly, did the fighting stop?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: It depended on the village concerned. In Ovnak somewhere on the early afternoon, whereas, in Strmac it was in the early evening, when I decided to withdraw from the Strmac position in order to evacuate the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time did the fighting stop in Grahovcici?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: It was only as night was falling, when the BH army forces carried out the last attack over Cekine Kuce, which is where all the civilians were located and being evacuated. But it wasn't possible to start the evacuation before night fell, because if they had been moved -- well, there were positions on both sides that the BH army occupied, from Han Bila and Rudnik and from surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you just told us that the BH army occupied. Can you tell us, did the BH army -- or what area the BH army occupied by nightfall, 8 June 1993.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: The inhabited places, Orasac, Cukle, Ovnak; a large part of Grahovcici had been taken; and in the evening hours the BH army took control of the entire area of Zupa and Brajkovici. That was about 13 Croatian villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from your elevated position, which of these areas could you physically see or were visible from where you were?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Ovnak was the place I could see the best, and Brajkovici, around the church. I could also see the constant evacuation, the passage of the civilians towards Rudnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe for the Trial Chamber what you saw in those areas that the BH army occupied as night fell on the 8th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: When the civilians were being evacuated in the afternoon, the shelling was very frequent. There was mortar shelling. And the BH army forces moved. They had already occupied certain inhabited places, so that the population was constantly under fire. The people spontaneously carried old people away and the wounded, and with the help of the civilian protection they evacuated the wounded in the evening. When the BH army forces took part of a village, usually they would set fire to one or two houses, if there was a group of five houses, and in the afternoon they would arrive in lorries, take away equipment, materiel, and technical equipment in the direction of Ovnak and then further on towards Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you just told us that they would usually set fire. Can you be more specific about any fires that you may have personally observed on the 8th of June, 1993, in what area or areas you personally saw that happening.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, in the early morning hours houses in Cukle were set on fire. I couldn't see who the owners of these houses were. I couldn't see whose houses they were, because it was at quite a distance afterwards, after Grahovcici and part of the Bilici hamlet had been taken. As soon as they had been taken, two or three houses were set on fire. And afterwards I was no longer able to see. As they advanced through the centre of the village of Grahovcici, they would occasionally set fire to a house or two. In each more densely inhabited hamlet, this is what would happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately what distance were you from the locations where houses were set on fire that you've described?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: I was about 200 metres from Bilici, as the crow flies. After moving from the position of Strmac to Plane I was again at a distance of about 2 or 3 hundred metres as the crow flies from the centre of the village, which is the most densely populated part of Grahovcici. And that is where all the refugees from the surrounding villages were located. And I saw that near Sikalo and Viktor Palavra and Zarko Bilic's houses were on fire, and I saw that many other houses and secondary facilities, barns, were also on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a clear line of sight as to these things which you've told us -- that you observed?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: It's very difficult to describe this. It's an elevated position from which you can see the entire area of Bila, not just my village. It was very easy to find a place from the position I was in, where I had a pair of binoculars. So it wasn't possible to fire at me, because this was a forested and hilly area. So for 10 or 15 minutes I would observe the situation quite frequently in order to see what was happening to the civilian population and how the evacuation was proceeding. And I would also observe that there were houses and secondary facilities in which were being torched.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, noting the time, it might be an appropriate time to take our recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's twenty to 4.00. We'll have a break of 25 minutes, and we shall resume at five past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution, can you please continue your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, immediately prior to the recess, you mentioned seeing several homes on fire. Do you know the source of the fires that you saw burning on the 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Some of those houses were torched; they were set fire to. One could clearly see that as soon as the troops approached those houses, they were set on fire. It is also possible that some were torched by various explosives and shells. In the course of that day, in that area that I could observe, about 20 houses and outbuildings were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you say that "as soon as the troops approached those housings, they were set on fire," can you tell us, tell the Chamber, what troops you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Those were soldiers belonging to the BH army, belonging to various units. From the distance, I could not see their insignia, so I couldn't tell exactly which units they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see, Witness, while the fighting was still going on, if any of the houses were on fire at that time; that is, while the fighting was still going on?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. I have already mentioned the owners of some of those houses which were on fire during the fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you distinguish between which houses were on fire during the fighting and which houses were set afire after the fighting had ended?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: All the houses were on fire in different times on the same day, and one could clearly see which houses were set ablaze once the village was taken by the BH army. Once the BH army approached those houses, they were set ablaze. Those that were not set ablaze by the troops could have been set on fire by the explosives during the fighting. Some two or three days - I couldn't see exactly, because I was wounded - but one could see clearly that some houses were set on fire even after the fighting in that area had stopped. We could see that from our reserve positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness, approximately how many houses or the owners of houses which were set on fire after the village was taken by the BH army and the fighting had stopped?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: In my village, the village where I resided at that time and where I currently reside, out of some 200 houses, bigger or smaller, during the war and after the war, only 5 per cent remained intact and the rest were either torched or were completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions for the witness at this time. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I give the floor to the Defence for the cross-examination, I would like to ask the witness: What was the distance between the houses that were set on fire exactly?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: I was some 50 metres or less away from some houses, as the crow flies. And as for the others, I was 2 or 3 hundred or even 5 hundred metres away from them. I could only see smoke coming from some of these houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you see around the houses that there were troops who set these houses on fire? How did the houses burn? How did the houses burn?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: The houses were set on fire during the taking of these settled areas, such as Nikolici, where the houses -- two houses were set ablaze immediately. And then there was also the village called Bilici, which was closest to me. Before the houses were set on fire, cattle was driven out of the outbuildings and barns. That I could see very clearly, because that was the closest I was to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before leaving the house, did the witness see his house burn? What was inside the house? Was the house evacuated before it was set ablaze?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: The house that were set on fire immediately upon the entry of the army were set ablaze with the complete interior, the contents of the houses were still there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say that you were between 50 to 100 metres from those houses and you didn't fire at them, at the troops that were entering the village?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Just in Nikolici, the houses where - we knew that the civilians had not all been evacuated. All the civilians who were there did not survive -- in Grahovcici, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That means that you fired at the enemy army?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. But this was out of the range of the houses. That was at a distance from the houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But still they could set these houses on fire, even if you fired at them.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: No, because we started withdrawing in the late afternoon hours towards the place from which we evacuated the civilians and we left all these houses behind. And as they approached the houses, they started setting some of those houses ablaze.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RASOAZANANY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to know whether there were amongst the troops of the BH army, whether there were any foreign soldiers, any mercenaries.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mujahedins from the strength of the 7th Muslim Unit were all present in the area at all times, especially around Mehurici, in the Bila region. Even before the conflict they would pass across Ovnak, in various vehicles that belonged to the BH army, and they would go to the positions towards Turbe, Bijelo Bucje and others. They were seen very often in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to give the floor to the Defence for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Jandric.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am Edina Residovic, representing General Hadzihasanovic. To the Prosecutor's question, you answered that already in April you joined the HVO and that from May onwards you were given a command duty; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war, in Travnik municipality there was the staff of the Territorial Defence, which, in case of a war, together with the JNA, would compose the armed forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The JNA and part of the Serb population in 1992 carried out an attack on Bosnia and Herzegovina; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In practical terms, it was only the Territorial Defence which remained as part of the legitimate defence forces, according to the then-prevailing regulations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know. What period of time are you referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The year 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: For a certain period of time the HVO troops also carried the insignia of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, the HVO was constituted as the military and political structure of the Croatian people before that time, during the attack on the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: The HVO was established in April 1992 as a military force of the Croatian people, but there were also Bosniaks and Serbs in that establishment, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, I believe that you will agree with me that although at that time in April 1992 the HVO did not exist pursuant to the regulations of Bosnia and Herzegovina, it proclaimed the joint goals of defending Bosnia against the aggressor.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: I was not a politician. I wasn't a politician then, and my only political option was to belong to the Reformist Party, and that's how I voted in the last elections in the BH. From then on I was never politically engaged, so I cannot answer that question. I cannot be the judge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate that. However, since you served in the army and you were a member of the HVO, you must be aware of the fact that sometime in 1992 the Law of Defence was passed and both the army and the HVO were proclaimed the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure how much further my learned colleague is going to go, but Prosecution would object to this line of questioning on the grounds of relevance and the fact that it goes beyond the scope of the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber state that is the question is of political nature and the witness is hereby asked to give his opinion on the political issues. The witness has answered by saying that he did have a political engagement; however, he missed one part of the question. You may pursue with this line of questioning; however, I believe that your question has already been answered. If you were to ask him whether there was the Croatian entity in Bosnia and Herzegovina, then this goes beyond the competence of this witness. However, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have already stated, I'm going to put these questions only, exceptionally, within the overall context of the events which are an integral part of the defence of General Hadzihasanovic, so I don't want to go into any details of this. I'm going to go into what the witness may be able to answer because he is aware of the facts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of the HVO already in the barracks in Travnik and later on as the commander of an HVO unit, you were absolutely aware of the fact that the HVO had its own line of command -- its own chain of command; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: During the time when I was in the barracks, we still had contacts, and it lasted until the beginning of conflicts with the BH army. At the higher level, commanders cooperated. In 1992, in May, I took about 90 people to a line in Stolac. They were from various units of the HVO Travnik, together with Major Petrovic, who was manning the line next to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Cooperation with the BH army units, as you have stated, in 1992 was still very good. However, I would like to ask you whether it is correct that already in October 1992 there were disagreements and discords in the relationships with the army and some armed conflicts around Prozor and Gornji Vakuf. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the Main Staff in autumn 1992 issued orders to the HVO to block roads for all the units except for the units of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: That may have only been after the murder of Ivica Stojak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are aware of such orders?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not, because up to then the BH army units would come to the lines of defence facing the Serbs. Personally, I never saw any such order. I never received an order to stop the BH army units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were appointed the commander of the company in Grahovcici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we are going to be talking about the area, I would like the witness to be shown a map of the area. We have enough copies for the Chamber and for the Prosecution. I believe that it is going to be easier for us to follow the witness's answers if we have the map before us. It is upside down, I'm afraid. Can you please turn the map the other way around. It is upside down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jandric, can you please show us Grahovcici on this map, where your unit was. Please look at the ELMO. And if you have a pen handy, can you please put a cross and a number "1" next to the village of Grahovcici.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would also kindly ask you to show us the Strmac elevation, where you were during the combat activities. Can you please put a cross next to it and put a number "2".

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that we have now marked Grahovcici by number 1 and that we have marked Strmac, the elevation at which you were during the combat activities by a number 2?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Strmac, you said, was the highest elevation above the Bila Valley. Can you please show us the Bila Valley region.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: The Bila is -- the Bila region is near the Bila River, the inhabited place. You can't see it from Miletici, Mehurici, and Jarsevac [phoen]. It's from there, always towards Nova Bila, through Han Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. To be quite clear, this is a more depressed geographical region than the one which is where you were at the time of the conflict, at the time of the fighting; is that correct? That was a valley that you could control, that you could view from that position; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I could control it visually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was at the same time a direction where you could also observe the civilian movements -- the civilian population which was being evacuated from the area caught up in the fighting.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: No. The civilian population, the direction they took when they were being evacuated, was towards Gornji Cukle and Ovnak, so it was in the opposite direction with regard to Grahovcici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But from Grahovcici, you said that they all arrived in Grahovcici and that they then headed in the direction of Bila.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: They came from Orasac through Cukle and arrived in Novo Selo and then Ovnak and then Grahovcici. They couldn't have gone to the Bila Valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, where did they go from Grahovcici?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: They could only go up to that collection point, which is where about 4 or 5 thousand civilians gathered, including women, children, and troops, and they could only continue at night. We waited for night to fall because the Bila Valley, there were inhabited places of Dolac and Rudnik, which were in the immediate vicinity of that collection point and this valley had been caught up in the fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the population finally set off in the direction of Dolac at night and then they continued towards the Lasva Valley; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: After one final attack, which was carried out at about 2000 hours since it was summer, and I managed to return with soldiers to positions and to stop the BH army members and prevent them from reaching the civilians -- at the same time, the people started moving towards Sarici over the bridge and they continued towards Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you now show me on the map where Cukle is. Could you mark this place with an "X" and number "3."

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This means that the place called Cukle is next to the number 3; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please show us where Susanj is. Please mark the place with a number "4."

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 4 indicates the place called Susanj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As opposed to the places in the Bila Valley which were below your position, is it correct to say that the north and north-eastern parts from the position in which you were located, would it be correct to say that these parts are mostly hilly areas, elevated areas?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it also be correct to say that the route you have shown from Susanj crossroads and onwards is a very important road? It connects Zenica and Travnik.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's one of the roads that existed between Zenica and Travnik. It's one of the roads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that as early as April, and especially in May, HVO units carried out significant fortification work in the area of Ovnak and in the Susanj area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: I didn't quite hear the period mentioned. Which year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the BH army took control of Zenica, in 1993. You said that after that you started carrying out fortification work. And my question is: Is it correct that those significant fortifications were erected in the area of this crossroads, in Ovnak, in the vicinity of the place called Susanj?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, not only at that site but throughout the entire area surrounding the Croatian villages. At that location and at that time there was a military police checkpoint, an HVO military police checkpoint from the Frankopan Brigade. And they controlled the Ovnak road. But at the time, no one used it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to that road, I'd like to ask you whether it would be correct to say that this -- the importance of this road was even greater because the road through the Lasva Valley was in fact blocked and it wasn't possible to use it.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. Before the conflict, in Zenica, one shift -- because of a misunderstanding and agreements between the army and the HVO, it was returned from the direction of Ovnak because on the certificate they had a destination indicated of Beljcevica [phoen], but they were directed towards Ovnak, and we only barely managed to avoid a clash.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will now return to what you were saying about your position. You said that in March 1993 or around that time in the area of Brajkovici, Nova Bila and Guca Gora, the Frankopan Brigade was formed at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: No. The Frankopan Brigade was formed from the so-called lower part of the municipality of Travnik, and it consisted of units from the inhabited places from Doci [phoen] or to Lasva and right up to the border of the municipality of Travnik. That means Grahovcici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that the command of the headquarters of the command were in -- of the brigade were in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: No, the main command of the Frankopan Brigade were in Nova Bila. But at the time of the conflict, the forward command post and the communications centre and the brigade operative offices were located in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the monastery in Guca Gora there was a communications and operations centre that belonged to the brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your unit before the brigade was established consisted of about 100 young armed men; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the beginning, these men were up to 35 or 40 years at the most, and they were engaged in all the positions at that time, with the Serbs too. And at the time of the conflict with the Bosniaks, a general mobilisation was proclaimed, and as a result there were older people who had also been engaged and assigned various tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jandric, you are certainly aware of the fact that in the area of Travnik and the villages around Travnik and Zenica, from 1992 a lot of refugees who had been expelled by the Serbian army arrived from the area of Krajina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. I also took care of such people in the barracks, and at the time we were at the plateau -- at the Vlasic Plateau buses would arrive and then they would be allowed to carry on towards Travnik. I don't know how they continued, but on the whole they were from Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you also aware of the fact that as early as November or December, after Jajce had fallen, there was a new wave of refugees that had arrived from the area of Jajce and Kotor Varos and from other places; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some of the refugees were provided with accommodation in abandoned houses in Brajkovici and Grahovcici, houses of people who were working abroad who left that area at the beginning of the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Most of those people did not accept accommodation in those places, although we were ready to provide them with such accommodation. Very few of them stayed on in the area of Brajkovici, and closer towards Han Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct to say that most of the Croatian refugees continued towards the Republic of Croatia and towards other places, whereas some of the Bosniak refugees stayed on in that area in Travnik and in Zenica? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't have all the information. All I know is that many of them remained in Busovaca, Vitez, Novi Travnik, if we're talking about Croatian refugees from Jajce and the surrounding places. As far as going to Croatia is concerned, I can't answer that question, since I don't have the information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After transferring from the Brigade Jure Francetic, you said that some of the soldiers came to the area that was under your control; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, another 200 or more men under arms came to your unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, but they didn't all stay on after they'd been accommodated with families in Busovaca and Vitez. They followed their families and they were assigned positions in the HVO in those places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You then received a significant amount of weapons, and this also included mortars and recoilless cannon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say that after that event your company was well armed and its strength was doubled or tripled; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: My company remained my company, and the command over the soldiers who had come from Zenica was Zeljko Ljubanic and the former commander of those units, they commanded them. We acted in a synchronised manner. They weren't under my direct command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to your fortifications and the trenches that you would dig to establish front lines, is it correct to say that there was a strong front line in the Brajkovici and Vrbica direction right up to the Strmica elevation, which is where you were on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those were precautionary measures that had been taken, but nothing special was done, since we didn't have any heavy weapons. These were ordinary, fortified trenches from Vrbica to Strmac and from Strmac to Ovnak, in that direction. It was in the immediate vicinity and in one part adjacent to the houses themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jandric, let's return to the map again. You said that you were at this elevation that we have marked with number 2. I think the scale of this map is 1 to 100.000. Do you know more about such maps than I do? The distance from Strmac to Cukle could be 5 or 6 centimetres on the map, and that means that in reality that would be 5 or 6 kilometres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your ability to see what was happening at such a distance was limited by the distance and also by the fact that the certain elevated areas in between; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was happening in the clashes around Cukle are thing that is you could only -- that you could just about make out. You could, as you said, hear the din of fighting and you could see smoke; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you already were well fortified at the crossroads in Surjan [phoen] and in this area towards Grahovcici, during those three days the BH army used a lot of artillery; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me now ask you something about the population that from Orasac and Podovi came towards Grahovcici. Is it correct to say that an order was issued on the initiative of the civilian protection according to which the population should be evacuated?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: No. In the course of the attack, from the places you have mentioned the people arrived spontaneously. There were constant attacks. They were trying to save their lives. An order from the civilian protection only arrived in the afternoon on the 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I wanted to ask you about. On the 8th of June, in the afternoon the civilian protection issued an order on evacuating the population.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the afternoon, when these people arrived in Grahovcici from the places that have already been mentioned. Many people died on the way from Cukle, Orasac, Podovi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Jandric, you can confirm that on the 8th of June the shelling was intense in that area, all day long.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can also confirm that your units resisted the attacks and returned fire and fired on the units attacking.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But they didn't move from the fortified front lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given the intense fighting which you have mentioned, as you said, it was possible for many buildings to catch fire as a result of all the firing.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally did not see a single soldier setting fire to a house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Not until they arrived in the inhabited place of Bilici and Nikolici. On that occasion I could see them with my naked eye. That's between 50 and 200 metres as the crow flies, and it is very visible from that elevation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at that time you also didn't see men setting the houses on fire. You just saw the soldiers leaving the houses.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: They were approaching the houses and immediately afterwards the house would start burning. They would then leave -- or move away from the house, approach another house, and carry on, continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that in the course of the fighting and after the fighting about 10 per cent of the houses had been set on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also know that several days after this fighting a special commission visited the area and determined what the situation in the area was. Are you aware of this fact?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the position that you were at and the reserve position, you were able to see hundreds of people, civilians with civilian vehicles, who were taking away -- who were leaving the houses with their goods; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Not on the first day, but there were large lorries, both civilian and military lorries, and they went in the direction of Ovnak alone. Afterwards, as far as what could be seen from the reserve position in Sarici, as far as what we could see from there, the situation developed which you have mentioned. But at the time there were very few civilians who remained in Grahovcici, and unfortunately as I have already said, very few civilians survived -- nobody survived, and thus it's not possible to testify about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You returned to Grahovcici in October 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 1st of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your house was still intact at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: It had been plundered and shepherds from Gornja Bukovica [phoen] were living in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, later on in 1995 it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. The roof and the roof construction were removed, but the users with their sheep and cattle were still in the house and they were using the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier on, you gave a statement to the Prosecution of the International Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were talking about things that you could best remember about these events.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that your company in Grahovcici, after the establishment of the Frankopan Brigade, had become the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion of this new brigade. The headquarters of the brigade were in Guca Gora and the commander was Ilija Nakic and Nakic replaced Filipovic as the commander of the Travnik Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. However, it was not the headquarters that was in Guca Gora, it was in Nova Bila, whereas, the forward command post and the operations unit were there. Ilija Nakic was not in Guca Gora. The headquarters of the Frankopan Brigade was in Nova Bila, in the sawmill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, what I've just read to you was what you stated to the Prosecutor during your interview, when you were giving the statement.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: I read the statement before I came to testify, and in the statement it says what I've just stated. Mr. Nakic would be in Guca Gora from time to time, but this was not the permanent headquarters. It was not in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. However, the communications centre of the brigade and the operations centre of the brigade were permanently in the monastery in Guca Gora; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the old part, in one part at the monastery, at the very entrance to the monastery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said to the OTP about the plundering of the houses that during the afternoon hours, from my position in Strmac I could see that the army units which passed through Brajkovici, Ovnak, and Milka were followed by Muslim civilians who entered these villages. These civilians came in lorries. They would load our cattle onto those lorries.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Not only lorries but also quite a lot of the equipment, tractor and military MTS and the personal belongings of the refugees had remained in Cukle, where there was the collection point of these refugees. From there then onwards conveys that were moving could be seen at all times moving into the villages from which the Croats had been expelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Jandric. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to give the floor to the Defence of Mr. Kubura. Cross-examined by Mr. Ibrisimovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jandric, I'm Fahrudin Ibrisimovic. I defend Mr. Kubura. I'm just going to ask you a few questions, because most of them have already been asked by me colleague. I would like you to tell us something about these events. As the commander of the Croatian Defence Council on the 8th of June you were in the forward command post in Strmac.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: I was forced to the command post and to the command post of the battalion, and then I would return to Sminjaca where the attack was going on throughout the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around 21.30, as you stated in your statement to the OTP, you moved to the reserve position in the Sarici village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: No, first I moved to the position in Plane, and from there I evacuated the civilians. And then around 2300 hours I crossed the bridge on the Bila River and I arrived in Sarici. Together with the civilians, I was carrying the wounded and the dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is across the Bila River, and it is about -- several kilometres from Grahovcici.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. And from the place where the collection point for the refugee Croats was, it was about 2 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from the area of Grahovcici and Brajkovici it is several kilometres; more than 2, in any case.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Sarici village is in the Bila River Valley?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: No. The Sarici village is the settled area called Kosovo Sarici [phoen] and it is uphill and borders on Brajkovici village. Some houses are even in the vicinity of the Bila River, but a lot of the house, most of the houses, are at an elevated ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sarici village is lower than Brajkovici and Grahovcici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that from that place you could not see -- on the following day you could not see what was going on in the area of Grahovcici, Brajkovici, Cukle, and those -- that area?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: I could see most of Grahovcici. The only part I couldn't see was the area around the school and the valley below Strmac. I could see complete Brajkovici, the church, Ovnak. I could see all that very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that because of the distance that was over 2 kilometres you personally could not see anybody plundering the belongings of the people?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: No, we couldn't. We could just recognise the convoys of vehicles and people who were moving about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you could not see from that distance that some of the soldiers of the BH army was setting the houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't. Although, on that day some houses were torched, but we could no longer see whether it was the civilians or the army who was setting these houses on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 9th of June you abandoned this area of Brajkovici and Grahovcici and that on the 12th of June, 1993 you left the area in which you were a commander and that you didn't return until the year 1994?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO JANDRIC
